narrative.headline: Top 50 skews decisively bullish — 25 of 50 names lean long with conviction concentrated in semis, retail, and financials, while defensive consumer and a few mega-cap tech names see distribution.

HD: flow 10.0 + $168M dark pool + strong blocks (8.36) — housing/retail conviction
JPM: flow 10.0 + $147M dark pool — financials being bid heavily
AVGO: $116M call premium + $173M dark pool — semis leadership confirmed by every component
KLAC/AMAT: paired semi-cap-equipment bullishness, both with flow >9.5 and dark pool >$134M
TSLA: $28M call premium + $179M dark pool — highest flow premium in the bullish cohort outside AVGO
AMZN: balanced 8.85/9.20/8.68 across all three components — broad institutional positioning
GEV: flow 10.0 + $98M dark pool — power/grid theme accumulation
PLTR: flow 8.61 + $99M dark pool — momentum name still being added

META: flow 2.95 with heavy dark pool — distribution in mega-cap tech

narrative.rotation_signal: Clear rotation INTO semis (AVGO/KLAC/AMAT/TXN), financials (JPM), industrials (CAT/GEV/RTX), and select retail (WMT/HD), and OUT OF defensive consumer (KO/COST), healthcare (LLY/UNH), payments (V), and surprisingly GOOG/META on the mega-cap tech side. The GOOGL bullish vs GOOG bearish split is notable — institutions are expressing the Alphabet view through the voting share.
narrative.diverging_from_industry_layer: LRCX bearish while AMAT and KLAC are top-5 bullish — unusual intra-semi-cap-equipment split worth flagging. GOOGL (bullish, score 8.03) vs GOOG (bearish, score 1.38) is a share-class divergence rarely seen and suggests targeted hedging or arb positioning rather than directional disagreement. XOM and GE registering flow 0.0 with bearish composites despite strong dark pool — energy/industrials may be diverging from the broader bullish industrial tape.
